title: Guardian decoy pack manifest v1
description: What a decoy pack is, declared. P2-W15 gave the decoy record nowhere to put a runtime detail — no image, command, mount, capability, or port field exists in the API, on the wire, or in the database — so this file is the only place one can enter, and it is committed rather than supplied by an operator. A manifest is a checked declaration, not a verified artefact: signature enforcement is the Phase 5 gate AC-SEC-004.

schema.description: The manifest contract version. A mismatch is explicit and fatal: a manifest this build does not implement is refused, never coerced and never partially read.

interaction_level.description: INT-01. SSH is medium, HTTP and SMB are low, a database surface may be either. High interaction is outside the MVP and has no value here.

ports.description: The ports the decoy answers on. A decoy presents a service; it does not choose its own address, which is P2-W1's business.

network.description: How the decoy is placed on the network. The mode is a closed set because each value is a capability the Edge must already implement; a manifest cannot invent a placement strategy.

mode.description: routed_secondary_ip is the P2-W1 MVP placement: a secondary address on a routed interface, reachable without touching production addressing. host_network is deliberately absent and is not a value this schema can express.

privileges.description: What the decoy needs beyond nothing. The default and the expectation is nothing: ADR 0009 and the P0-W6 review established a baseline of dropped capabilities, read-only root, no bind mounts, no runtime sockets, and no-new-privileges, and this object cannot express a departure from any of those. A request outside the closed capability set is rejected at load rather than filtered, so a pack author never believes they were granted something they were not.

capabilities.description: Linux capabilities to add to an otherwise empty set. NET_BIND_SERVICE is the only one Guardian grants, and only because a decoy presenting SSH on 22 or HTTP on 80 has no other way to bind it. Nothing here can request CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_NET_ADMIN, CAP_NET_RAW, or privileged mode; there is no value for them.

telemetry.description: How the pack's events reach the canonical envelope. The adapter is named from a closed set because each value is code that must exist; P2-W10 and P2-W11 own the normalisation.

health_probe.description: How P2-W14 decides whether this decoy is functionally alive. A probe is a connection attempt against a declared port and nothing more: it must not be able to run a command, because a health check that executes something is a second execution path into the decoy.

resources.description: Bounds the runtime applies. Required, not optional: an unbounded decoy is a denial-of-service surface on the host that is supposed to be protecting the network.

egress.description: AC-SEC-003. The default policy denies outbound traffic to a forbidden external destination, and a manifest declares only what it needs on top of that. There is no 'allow all' value and no wildcard destination: the absence of a declaration means nothing is permitted, never everything. Cowrie is medium-interaction software and this is the field that keeps it from reaching the internet.

policy.description: deny is the only policy. It is written out rather than assumed so that a reader of the manifest sees it, and so that adding a second value is a schema change with a review attached.

allow.description: Exceptions to the deny. Empty for every MVP pack: a decoy that needs to reach something is a decoy that can be used to reach something.

destination.description: One RFC1918 host address. A public destination cannot be expressed.

persona.description: DC-11 content metadata: what the pack presents to whoever probes it. Bounded text only. It cannot name a file, a path, a template, or a command, because content that can name an artefact is a second way to get one into the decoy.

personas.description: The curated DC-11 personas this pack can present. A decoy's persona must be one of these, and the set is closed: there is no generative persona builder, and AIM-06 places one outside the MVP.

hostname_pattern.description: The shape of the hostname the decoy presents. Attacker-visible by design, so it must never resemble a real host: it is a pattern for generating a plausible name, not a name copied from the network.

banner.description: Bounded text the service presents on connection. Attacker-visible by design and therefore never a real version string, a real hostname, or anything identifying a real system.
